Subject: Sizing & SKU options for Dedicated deployment (OrbisAI pilot)

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited to pilot Redwood Dedicated for our on-prem-sensitive customers. Before we lock in the reserved capacity, procurement wants a short write-up on which GPU SKUs you recommend and why — they care about long-context LLMs (30k tokens) for some of our models, but we also have a large volume of inference traffic for shorter prompts.

High-level asks from Orbis procurement/infra:
- Guidance on memory vs throughput tradeoffs (H100 vs A100 vs L4)
- Rough per-token latency expectations for 2k, 8k, and 30k contexts
- Fallback strategy if H100 capacity is constrained (cost impact)
- Any quantization/compatibility caveats for our models (we use llama-family & some T5-based encoders)

Can you send a recommended fleet mix and a simple ops note we can share with our internal infra and SRE? Procurement also asked for an SLA callout if dedicated is required.

Best,
Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering
OrbisAI

Camila / Aditya — attached is a first-pass fitment matrix (sku_fitment_matrix_v1.xlsx) and an executive one-pager below. I kept it intentionally terse for procurement.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- H100 (best for long-context, highest peak throughput per-GPU for FP16/AMP; recommended for models that need >80GB effective KV/cache or 30k token contexts). Operational caveat: higher unit cost, lower per-dollar throughput for short requests.
- A100 80GB (sweet spot for mixed workloads): good memory and throughput balance, more cost-efficient than H100 for many production models, handles 8k contexts well, simpler compatibility with existing quantization pipelines.
- L4 (inferentia-like cost-efficient GPU): best for low-memory, high-concurrency short prompts (2k token typical). Low memory makes long-context models impractical unless you shard or use KV-cache offload.

Recommended starter fleet for Orbis pilot (based on your described mix — 20% long-context heavy, 60% short/interactive, 20% batch/embeddings):
- Reserve: 6x H100 (for peak long-context capacity & can serve as overflow for mixed loads)
- Reserve: 12x A100-80GB (primary serving layer for mixed load; handles majority of requests)
- Reserve: 18x L4 (cost-efficient front tier for short prompts + embeddings)

Fallback and hedging:
- Auto-fallback policy: route long-context to A100 at reduced concurrency with KV-cache warmup when H100 saturated; route short traffic from A100 -> L4 when coupled with quantization and shorter sequence length.
- Savings option: enable 4-bit quantized variants on A100/L4 for short requests to reduce cost per token (we can produce model-specific latency delta numbers).

Attachments: sku_fitment_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

Next steps: Aditya — can you add per-token latency estimates for the 2k/8k/30k contexts and note any quantization compatibility issues for LLaMA-family + T5 encoders? I’ll prepare this for Sanjay and procurement.

Ben
Solutions Engineering

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing & SKU options for Dedicated deployment (OrbisAI pilot)

Ben / Camila — quick tech addendum for Sanjay (cc’d in the next outbound):

1) Latency ballpark (P95) per-token estimates, typical infra config (single-GPU single-request, FP16 where applicable):
   - 2k context: L4 ~ 1.1–1.6 ms/token; A100 ~ 0.8–1.2 ms/token; H100 ~ 0.7–1.0 ms/token
   - 8k context: L4 becomes memory-bound for larger models (expect memory/fatal unless using offload); A100 ~ 1.5–2.5 ms/token; H100 ~ 1.1–1.8 ms/token
   - 30k context: A100 will need careful KV/cache partitioning and may require model sharding depending on model architecture; H100 recommended — H100 ~ 2.8–4.5 ms/token (depends heavily on attention implementation)

2) Memory/compatibility notes:
   - LLaMA-family: works well with 4-bit quantization on A100/L4 for shorter contexts; for 30k contexts we recommend H100 or A100-80GB with KV offload.
   - T5-style encoders: tokenization and encoder attention patterns generally cheaper (lower memory per token) — often can fit into A100 for mid-length contexts.

3) KV-cache strategy and ops implications:
   - Warm KV cache is crucial for latency goals on long-context workloads; recommend a cache-warmup policy in Redwood routing and a pre-warm window on H100 nodes for scheduled high-load periods.
   - For H100 shortage, fallback to A100 with reduced concurrency; include automatic throttling to avoid OOMs. This increases per-token latency (roughly +20–60% depending on model).

4) Quantization caveats:
   - L4 best-effort quantization path varies by model; we should test your checkpoint set. Some T5 variants show quality regressions at 4-bit for long-context runs. We should run a small eval set (we can do this under the pilot).

I’ll push detailed microbench numbers to the shared Drive link after we run Orbis-specific checkpoints. For now these are conservative ranges based on our internal clusters.

— Aditya
Senior ML Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: OrbisAI pilot - recommended GPU fleet mix and edge-case sizing

Hi Sanjay — attaching our recommended starter fleet and a short ops note (spreadsheet link below). We aligned the recommendation to the mix you described (20% long-context, 60% short/interactive, 20% batch/embeddings).

Recommendation summary (same as internal):
- Reserve 6x H100: primary platform for 30k-context models and for warm KV-cache heavy flows
- Reserve 12x A100-80GB: main serving layer for mixed workloads, best cost/compat for most checkpoints
- Reserve 18x L4: front-tier for high-concurrency short prompts and cheaper embeddings

What this means for Orbis procurement and SRE:
- SLA: Redwood Dedicated offers reserved capacity and an SLA for uptime and latency targets. For long-context SLA commitments (30k token P95 latency), we recommend reserving the H100 pool to avoid fallbacks during peak.
- Ops: enable KV-cache warmup for scheduled peak windows; add autoscaling headroom of ~20% to handle burst; implement routing rules: long-context -> H100 preferred; mixed -> A100; short -> L4 (with quantized variants where acceptable).

Links & artifacts:
- SKU fitment spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_orbis_sku_matrix (contains per-token estimate table + cost model)
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890

Attachments referenced: sku_fitment_matrix_v1.xlsx, orbis_sla_requirements.pdf

If this looks good I’ll send a one-page for procurement (with the recommended reserved counts and a short cost delta table) and a proposal for an initial 8-week pilot (benchmarks + model-specific evals). Can you confirm target budget band and any blackout dates for pilot infra?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
